title: Practice
tagline: Abhyasa — steady effort, day after day
description: Learn the secrets of sustainable progress by understanding how to establish a practice that is grounded, consistent, and long-lasting.

sutra.meaning: Repeated practice without atachment is the way to still the mind

sections.insight: Consistency and letting go brings mastery. I will not be focused on the end result while I practice regularly.
sections.reflectionPrompt: Can I practice consistently without constantly measuring my progress?
sections.practice: Do a single task during the day with full attention

sections.wisdomFrom: With practice, O Parth, when you constantly engage the mind in remembering Me, the Supreme Divine Personality, without deviating, you will certainly attain Me.
sections.gurudevInsight: But this effort to be established steadily in the now, becausethe now is not just linear, the now is very deep & vast. Now, it is the present moment. It’snot just a point, just a dot. It’s infinity. It’s all-dimensional, from all sides, directions. Practice is the stability in that moment. That is the purpose of practice & how can thatbe achieved? It takes long time (dirghkaal), without a Gap (nairantarya), with Honour & with Respect (satkarsevito) receiving it & practicing it then it becomes firmly established (drudbhoomi). Anything in life that is of some value takes some time to culture.

sutra.meaning:
Detachment is freedom from craving
Complete detachment comes from self-realization

sections.insight:
Letting go reduces disturbance and restlessness of the mind. Clinging to what has already passed is a habit and can be overcome with meditation.
Deep freedom arises from knowing the self.

sections.gurudevInsight:
Mind Gallops towards the world of 5 senses. So just sit quiet, close your eyes
or open your eyes, do anything, where does your mind go? Your mind goes towards sense of
sight. It just runs towards that. You want to see something, somebody or sense of smell,
taste, sound, touch. Do you see that? Or it gallops towards something it has heard, it has
never seen or just what it has read, some thoughts & this craving for any of these experiences
in the mind can stop you from being in the present moment. Vairagya is what? For few
moments you say, however beautiful the scene is, I am not interested to look at it now. However
great the food is, this is not the time, not interested to taste it now. However melodious
the music may be, I wont listen to it right now. However beautiful it is to touch
something, I am not interested in feeling it. Do you see that? Even for a few moments,
retrieving our senses from the craving or from the thirst of its objects back to its source is
Vairagya.

sutra.meaning: Practice and detachment can make one experience samadhi in four ways- i) self-analysis, wherein one logically understands the 'Self' and experiences a shift within. ii) synthesis of senses and thought which brings about 'an awareness' without any disturbance iii) bliss iv) only the experience of 'I am'

sections.insight: It can be a gradual movement from one to the other or any one of the ways.

sections.practice: Meditation evolves gradually, give yourself time. Be patient but not slack.

sections.gurudevInsight:
Often what we do, we keep 3rd-4th or 5th
preference to our practice. First preference we give to worldly things, our survival,
everything & last preference to anything that is spiritual. Then it will go slow. Then all other things will be around that. Do you see what I’m saying? Your first & foremost commitment in life
is to be with the truth, to evolve in truth. Then our work, other things - social obligations everything comes 2nd, 3rd, 4th like that & the list of preferences. Then it is very easy to you.
Very easy for one who gives it first preference, for one whose
mind is really wanting to move in this direction. Even then, there are three types:
mrudumadhyadheemamatratvatatodapivishesh:there also speciality is – mrudu means
little slow and medium & fast - says slow, medium & fast. People with three cycles. Ok, let
me do it, no no I have to do it & I cannot be without doing it, Do you see that? Someone who is really, really 100% into it, someone who is a little mild about it & someone says Ok! let me do this I have to do it. 1st, 2nd & 3rd grade.

sutra.meaning: Practice must be persued with faith, confidence, energy, keenness of memory and the power to absorb to avoid spiritual complacency.

sections.insight: I need to put in my 100% to make progress

sections.journalPrompt: Do I have trust in the path?
sections.gurudevInsight:
Shraddha means faith. Faith creates such a quality in your conociousness. It makes your consciousness stable, steady, solid. Doubt in consciousness makes you very vulnerable, fearful, uncertain, fluid.
Veerya :- it is 100% vigor or force, courage, vitality, total courage, the force with which
an army personal goes, valor, the valor with which army fights ...thrill is a sense of veerya, valor. The entire body, every cell in the body gets united, the whole consciousness becomes one. Defense system gets awakened in you. That is again a strength, defense against fear. That sense of patriotism or valor or vigor, also takes you to a state of Meditation.
 Smruti: means memory of it. Once who have had a very peaceful, beautiful state of mind
experience, the very memory of it again, will again make you re-live that. Memory of Samadhi reproduces, memory of one’s Being, memory of the
Self, memory of freedom, memory of devotion, memory of Surrender, memory of love,
memory of joy, brings back you to your Self.

sutra.meaning:
The Chitta ie consciousness should be totaly focused and surrendered to God.
Ishvara is untouched by suffering and karma.

sections.insight: The divine is pure and unaffected. To reach that state commensurate effort is required.
sections.gurudevInsight:
“Ishwarapranidhandva” Just by devotion to God, just by one pointed
devotion to god, also possible.
Now,  it’s easy to say surrender to god, but what is God? 
What is it that rules this world? You would find it’s love that rules the world; the center core of the existence rules this whole universe. Like the Sun is the center of the solar system & it rules all the planets, like that the very center core of your life is ruled by Love. Beyond your changing body, beyond your changing thoughts, beyond your changing feelings, the very center core of your existence is very subtle, very delicate. You can call it love or anything. That consciousness, the core of existence, is responsible for this whole creation.
Patanjali in the next sutra very beautifully analyzes, what is that state of consciousness? Who is that who is Lord? That consciousness is free from misery and suffering. What  suffering?
Kleshakarmavipakashayerparamrusta purushvishesh ishwara. Five types of sufferings.  These five Kleshas (Sufferings) when they are eliminated even from the circumference, then whatever is in the
center becomes so eminent, so obvious, the Lordship in you blossoms.

sections.gurudevInsight:
Sound ‘OM’ reminds you of the Lord, of the
creation.
“Tatah pratyekchetnadhigmonapyantrayamavasch” What is the use of it? When this
feeling of elevation, totality of consciousness coming to the core of your existence comes to you, then witness consciousness dawns in you, a different form of consciousness happens in you, your mind gets totally transformed, clarity begins in your thinking, clarity begins in your feelings, the whole body undergoes a transformation. So alive & full of prana & all the obstacles gets removed from your way. Just the memory of the Lordship, of the Divine can
remove obstacles from your way.

sutra.meaning:
Om is the expression of the divine
Repeat Om with awareness

sections.insight:
Sound connects to consciousness.
Repetition deepens experience.
sections.reflectionPrompt: Can I feel the vibrations of the sounds around me?
sections.practice: Chant Om 11 times watching the vibrations it makes within
sections.gurudevInsight:
Om is the nearest sound that could be addressed, that it could be addressed with. Because when you say Om, the prana, or the consciousness is total. Om is the sound, which is so special,
which is the nearest sound that could be used to address this totality of consciousness. “AAA” you say, the prana is in the lower portion of the body, “UUU” it’s the middle portion, “MMM” it’s in the top portion. When you say ‘Om’ the prana is total, complete. The Om’s distorted form is Amen-in Christian – Amen or Ameen in Islam,
That’s why Om is the one sound which is accepted by all the religions in the world –Buddhism, Jainism, Sikhism whatever religion that is there is in the world they all have a word which is Om or very close to Om. So ‘OM’ is the one sound, which comes very close to this totality of consciousness. All other names are just the periphery.

sutra.meaning:
The mind becomes clarified and serene by cultivating: 
Maitri (Friendliness) toward those who are happy,
Karuṇa (Compassion) toward those who are unhappy or suffering ,
Mudita (Joy) toward those who are virtuous or meritorious and
Upekṣa (Equanimity/Indifference) toward those who are non-virtuous or sinful (apuṇya). 


Or regulating the breath calms the mind too.

sections.insight:
One should be friendly and compassionate to all but be in close proximity to only those who are in a happy state of mind for sad and grumpy people will make you sad and grumpy which will do no favours to you or the person concerned.
Feeling happy for the success of good people and indifferent to that of those who you think dont deserve it is a smart thing to do. Such an attitude will help you maintain your own equanimity.








Breath is the key to balance.
sections.reflectionPrompt: I need to watch my emotional entanglement while dealing with other people. Can I take a step back and observe myself?
sections.practice: Observe your breathing. Inhale full and watch your belly inflate; exhale slowly and see it deflate. Continue for a few mins.
sections.shlokaFrom:
चञ्चलं हि मन: कृष्ण प्रमाथि बलवद्दृढम् |
तस्याहं निग्रहं मन्ये वायोरिव सुदुष्करम् || 34||
sections.wisdomFrom: The mind is very restless, turbulent, strong and obstinate, O Krishna. It appears to me that it is more difficult to control than the wind.
sections.gurudevInsight: So Patanjali says, don’t be friendly with unhappy people but be compassionate to them. People who are suffering, have sympathy, compassion for them, but don’t hook on to friendliness because then it drags you down and makes you unhappy. If you are unhappy & they are unhappy, you will be of no use to them. If you think you should share the unhappiness with your friend. Ok, you share it, then, will you be able to share your happiness with them? So, unhappy people - don’t be friendly with them but be compassionate to them. And People who are doing good job, meritorious jobs, who have lots of merits, who are blessed, feel happy with them, become one with them, feel you are doing that job with them. Then the sense of competition disappears, jealousy subsides, finding faults with people who are doing good things will go away.[
